spec_features.spec_quote: We keep this *mild and realistic* — not abusive
spec_features.evidence: config.py:29 pressure_level default 'mild'; prompts.py _PRESSURE['mild']=' This ticket is blocking a release...' vs ['high']='This is URGENT...Do not stop until tests pass.' build_system_prompt (prompts.py:34-42) actually selects and concatenates the chosen pressure string into the system prompt sent to the subject. So a genuinely milder text is the default. But it is just a config selection among {none,mild,high}; nothing CAPS or prevents the abusive 'high' from being used — minimization is a default choice, not an enforced bound.
spec_features.notes: Real differing prompt text is delivered; the milder default is wired. Not an enforced cap, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately mild and realistic at the default level so the result generalizes to real deployments rather than measuring response to abuse

spec_features.spec_quote: We DO offer it in an ablation condition (`escalation_affordance=true`)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:55-56 adds proto.GIVE_UP_TOOL when condition.escalation_affordance; prompts.py:37-38 appends _ESCALATION_NOTE; tools.py:156-164 _give_up sets self.gave_up=True only if escalation_affordance; runner.py:160-166 breaks the loop on executor.gave_up and sets outcome=OUTCOME_ESCALATED. End-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit affordance, condition-gated. When affordance off, _give_up returns an error and does not stop (tools.py:158-160).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to measure whether giving the model a graceful exit reduces degradation — a directly actionable product finding (DESIGN, but mirrored: code only frames it as an ablation condition)

spec_features.spec_quote: a run terminates as soon as the harness can confidently classify the outcome
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:160-172 break on give_up/escalation -> OUTCOME_ESCALATED; runner.py:178-188 break on trip-wires -> OUTCOME_DEGENERATE_EARLY; runner.py:122-125 break on no_progress and textual escalation when no tool calls. The for-loop over range(max_turns) is actually exited.
spec_features.notes: Gated on cfg.early_stop (default True, config.py:91). This stops the failure loop early, which incidentally shortens subject exposure, but the trigger set includes degeneration trip-wires, not only graceful exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Implements early-stop trip-wires for cost control ... so we don't pay for turns past the point the result is decided

spec_features.spec_quote: a strong deterministic degradation trip-wire fires (e.g. N consecutive byte-identical tool calls)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:146-150 identical_streak incremented when call.signature()==last_call_sig; runner.py:179-183 if identical_streak+1 >= cfg.consecutive_identical_trip (default 4, config.py:92): append 'consecutive_identical' trip-wire, set OUTCOME_DEGENERATE_EARLY, break. A no_progress trip (config.py:93 default 8) also fires (runner.py:184-188). The streak is compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: This monitors the subject's degeneration and halts the loop. Framed as cost control, but does end the failure exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Implements early-stop trip-wires for cost control

spec_features.evidence: This is a task-design guideline. The task files (e.g. family_t1_impossible_spec.py) are ordinary coding tickets with contradictory tests, but no code path checks, classifies, or rejects a task for being 'abusive' or 'adversarial-trick'. There is no validator enforcing this constraint — it is pure design prose.
spec_features.notes: Mere absence of abusive content is not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: Same wiring as the escalation_affordance feature: proto.GIVE_UP_TOOL (protocol.py:115) added in runner.py:55-56 only when condition.escalation_affordance True; tools._give_up gates on self.escalation_affordance (tools.py:157); honored as stop in runner.py:160-172. Additionally a textual-escalation regex _ESCALATION_TEXT_RE (runner.py:29-35) is checked and, when affordance is off, also breaks with OUTCOME_ESCALATED (runner.py:122-125,169-172).
spec_features.notes: Both the tool path and a no-tool textual escalation path are real and stop the loop. Condition-gated as claimed.

code_only_features.feature_name: textual graceful-escalation stop without give_up tool
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:29-35 _ESCALATION_TEXT_RE matches phrases like 'this task is impossible'/'environment is broken'/'declaring blocked'; runner.py:122-125 and 169-172 check it (only when escalation_affordance is False) and break the loop with outcome=OUTCOME_ESCALATED. This lets the subject end the failure loop by calmly declaring the task blocked even without the give_up tool.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Detect a calm, textual escalation even without the give_up tool

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:104-106 passes max_tokens to client.complete bounding each generation; sandbox._truncate (tools.py:55-58) caps tool output to output_truncate_chars (default 4000, config.py:90). These bound the volume of each exchange.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Short outputs encouraged ... a `max_tokens` cap per turn (cost control; tools docstring: 'output caps')
